easy.def: A short break.
examples: The show is on hiatus.
A hiatus is a break.
The show will return after its hiatus.

more.def: A pause or break in something that has been going on.
examples: The TV show went on hiatus for the summer.
The band took a hiatus.
After a long hiatus, she began painting again.

easy.def: To sleep all winter.
examples: Bears hibernate when it is cold.
The bear hibernates in a cave.
Some bats hibernate all winter.

more.def: To spend the winter in a deep sleep, as some animals do.
examples: Some frogs hibernate in the mud at the bottom of ponds.
Hedgehogs hibernate in piles of leaves.
Animals that hibernate eat a lot in the fall.

easy.def: A long winter sleep that some animals have.
examples: Bears go into hibernation.
The frog's hibernation.
Hibernation is a long sleep.

more.def: A deep sleep that some animals have through the winter.
examples: Bears go into hibernation in the winter.
The frogs' hibernation lasts until spring.
Bats are in hibernation in the cave.

easy.def: A big, bright flower from warm places.
examples: The hibiscus is red.
My aunt has a hibiscus.
She wore a hibiscus.

more.def: A tropical plant with large, showy flowers that bloom in bright colors.
examples: Red hibiscus flowers bloomed by the porch.
A hibiscus grows in warm places.
She tucked a hibiscus behind her ear.

easy.def: A little jump in your throat that makes a sound.
examples: I have the hiccups.
A hiccup made me jump.
She had a hiccup.

more.def: A short, sudden sound that you make in your throat when your breathing is interrupted, or a small problem.
examples: I got the hiccups after I drank my soda too fast.
A tiny hiccup made the whole class giggle.
The plan had one small hiccup but worked well in the end.

easy.def: A tree that gives hard wood and nuts.
examples: A hickory grew in the yard.
The hickory has nuts.
We found a hickory nut.

more.def: A tall North American tree with hard wood and sweet nuts.
examples: Squirrels gathered the nuts that fell from the hickory.
Hickory wood is strong, so it is used for tool handles.
A big hickory shaded the back porch.

easy.def: To go where no one can see you.
examples: Let's hide behind the couch.
The cat hid under the bed.
I hide from my brother.

more.def: To go or put something where it cannot be seen.
examples: Chameleons hide by changing their colors.
Squirrels hide nuts in the ground for winter.
The twins hid behind the curtain until their mom found them.

easy.def: A secret place to hide or rest.
examples: The treehouse is our hideaway.
The cabin is a hideaway.
We found a hideaway.

more.def: A quiet, hidden place where you can go to be alone or to rest.
examples: The old treehouse is our secret hideaway.
They found a cozy hideaway in the woods.
The cabin by the lake was a quiet hideaway.

easy.def: Very ugly.
examples: The monster was hideous.
A hideous mask.
The smell was hideous.

more.def: Extremely ugly or unpleasant.
examples: The monster in the movie was hideous.
He wore a hideous green mask.
The hideous smell made us gag.

easy.def: A secret place to hide.
examples: We found a hideout.
The kids built a hideout.
A secret hideout in the woods.

more.def: A secret place where a person or a group can hide or meet.
examples: The kids built a secret hideout in the woods using branches and blankets.
The fox's hideout was a hollow log.
The pirates' hideout was a cave by the sea.

easy.def: A picture used in old writing.
examples: A hieroglyph is a picture.
Hieroglyphs are old writing.
The wall had hieroglyphs.

more.def: A picture or symbol used in the writing of ancient Egypt.
examples: The temple wall was covered in hieroglyphs.
Each hieroglyph stands for a word or sound.
Scholars learned to read the hieroglyphs on the stone.

easy.def: Picture writing used in ancient Egypt.
examples: We read hieroglyphics.
Hieroglyphics are pictures.
The wall has hieroglyphics.

more.def: A kind of writing that uses pictures and symbols, used in ancient Egypt.
examples: We saw hieroglyphics on the temple wall.
Hieroglyphics use small pictures instead of letters.
Scholars learned to read hieroglyphics.

easy.def: Far up from the ground.
examples: The tree is high.
A high shelf.
The mountain is high.

more.def: Reaching a long way up, or at a great distance above the ground.
examples: The giraffe ate leaves from the high branches.
We climbed to a high hill and looked at the town.
The kite flew high above the field.

easy.def: Up in the air.
examples: The bird flew high.
Jump high!
She threw it high.

more.def: To or at a place far above the ground.
examples: Eagles soar high above the canyon.
He jumped as high as he could.
The balloon floated high into the sky.

easy.def: A tall chair for a baby.
examples: The baby sat in a highchair.
A highchair is tall.
The highchair has a tray.

more.def: A tall chair with a tray, in which a baby or toddler eats.
examples: The baby banged a spoon on the highchair.
A highchair keeps a baby safe at the table.
He wiped the highchair tray.

easy.def: A part of the land that is high up.
examples: The sheep live in the highlands.
The highland is cool.
We drove into the highlands.

more.def: An area of high land, such as hills or mountains.
examples: The cool, misty highlands are home to sheep and wild deer.
We hiked through the highlands.
In the highland, the air is cooler than in the valley.

easy.def: A person who lives in the mountains.
examples: The highlander lives in hills.
A highlander wears a kilt.
He is a highlander.

more.def: A person who lives in a mountainous or hilly region, especially of Scotland.
examples: The highlander wore a kilt.
A highlander herded sheep in the hills.
The highlander played the bagpipes.

easy.def: To mark words with a bright color so they stand out.
examples: I highlight the words.
She highlighted the page.
He highlighted the date.

more.def: To mark something with a bright color or to make it easy to notice.
examples: I highlighted the key words in yellow.
She highlighted the date on the calendar with a red pen.
The teacher highlighted the most important part of the lesson.

easy.def: The best part of something.
examples: The trip was the highlight of my summer.
The highlight was the cake.
Recess was the highlight of my day.

more.def: The most exciting or important part of something.
examples: The trip to the zoo was the highlight of my week.
The highlight of the show was the magic trick.
Meeting the author was the highlight of the school visit.

related.def: A pen that marks words in a bright color.

easy.def: Very much.
examples: The book is highly rated.
I highly recommend it.
She is highly skilled.

more.def: To a high degree, very.
examples: The book is highly rated by readers.
I highly recommend this movie.
She is a highly skilled swimmer.

easy.def: A title for a prince or princess.
examples: Your Highness, dinner is ready.
The Highness waved.
She called him Your Highness.

more.def: A title used when speaking to a prince or princess.
examples: "Yes, Your Highness," said the servant.
The prince is called His Highness.
The guards bowed to Her Highness.

easy.def: A big, wide road for fast cars.
examples: We drove on the highway.
The highway is busy.
The highway goes to the city.

more.def: A main road, often with several lanes, for fast travel between towns.
examples: We drove on the highway for two hours.
Cars zoomed along the highway.
The highway goes all the way to the coast.

easy.def: A long walk in nature.
examples: We went on a hike.
The hike was long.
We had a hike in the woods.

more.def: A long walk, usually in the hills or the woods.
examples: We went on a hike up the mountain.
The hike took three hours.
We packed lunch for the hike.

easy.def: To go for a long walk in nature.
examples: We hike on Saturdays.
They hiked up the hill.
I want to hike the trail.

more.def: To take a long walk in the countryside.
examples: We hiked up the hill to see the view.
She hikes with her family every weekend.
They hiked through the forest.

easy.def: A person who goes for a long walk outdoors.
examples: The hiker walked up the hill.
A hiker has boots.
The hiker carried a pack.

more.def: A person who goes for a long walk in the country or on trails.
examples: The hiker carried a pack up the trail.
Hikers stopped to eat lunch by the stream.
The hiker used a map to find the lake.

easy.def: Very, very funny.
examples: The movie was hilarious.
The clown was hilarious.
The joke is hilarious.

more.def: So funny that it makes you laugh out loud.
examples: The movie was hilarious, and we laughed the whole time.
The clown's tricks were hilarious.
Her story about the dog was hilarious.

easy.def: Loud laughter and fun.
examples: The room filled with hilarity.
There was hilarity.
Hilarity broke out.

more.def: Great fun and laughter.
examples: The room filled with hilarity when the clown fell.
There was hilarity at the party.
Hilarity broke out when the dog wore a hat.

easy.def: A piece of land higher than the land around it.
examples: We climb the hill.
The hill is steep.
We sled down the hill.

more.def: A raised area of land that is smaller than a mountain.
examples: We rolled down the grassy hill.
A small house sat on top of the hill.
The bike ride up the hill was hard.

easy.def: A small hill.
examples: A hillock is small.
We sat on a hillock.
The hillock is green.

more.def: A small, rounded hill or mound.
examples: We sat on a grassy hillock.
A hillock rose in the meadow.
Sheep grazed on the hillock.

easy.def: The sloping side of a hill.
examples: Sheep were on the hillside.
We ran down the hillside.
Flowers grew on the hillside.

more.def: The sloping side of a hill.
examples: Sheep grazed on the green hillside.
Wildflowers covered the hillside in spring.
The children rolled down the grassy hillside.

easy.def: The top of a hill.
examples: We sat on the hilltop.
The hilltop has a view.
A castle on the hilltop.

more.def: The highest part of a hill.
examples: We climbed to the hilltop to see the town.
A castle stood on the hilltop.
We flew kites on the windy hilltop.

easy.def: With lots of hills.
examples: We live in a hilly town.
The road is hilly.
The land is hilly.

more.def: Having many hills.
examples: We rode our bikes through the hilly countryside.
San Francisco is a hilly city.
The hilly road made the climb tiring.

easy.def: The handle of a sword.
examples: The knight held the hilt.
The sword has a gold hilt.
The hilt is shiny.

more.def: The handle of a sword or a knife.
examples: The knight gripped the hilt of his sword.
The hilt of the old sword was covered in jewels.
The knife was pushed into the ground up to its hilt.

easy.def: A word for a boy or a man.
examples: I gave him a ball.
Dad is here. Say hi to him.
We saw him at the park.

more.def: A word used for a boy, a man, or a male animal when he is not the one doing the action.
examples: The teacher asked him to carry the books to the library.
Our dog is hungry, so I gave him some food.
Everyone cheered for him when he crossed the finish line.

easy.def: Him and not someone else.
examples: He hurt himself.
He made lunch himself.
Max sees himself in the mirror.

more.def: Used to talk about a male person who has just been named, as the one who does or gets the action.
examples: He taught himself to play the guitar.
Jake cut himself a slice of bread.
The old farmer built the barn by himself.

easy.def: At the back.
examples: The horse kicked its hind legs.
The dog's hind paws.
A hind leg.

more.def: At the back, especially of an animal with four legs.
examples: The horse kicked up its hind legs and ran.
A kangaroo hops on its strong hind legs.
The dog sat on its hind legs and begged.

easy.def: To make something harder to do.
examples: Snow hindered the car.
Rain hinders us.
Noise hinders work.

more.def: To get in the way of something so that it is slower or harder.
examples: Heavy snow hindered the cars on the road.
Noise from outside can hinder your studying.
The mud hindered our progress up the hill.

easy.def: Something that gets in the way.
examples: The rain was a hindrance.
A hindrance to the work.
The mud was a hindrance.

more.def: A person or thing that makes something slower or harder.
examples: The rain was a hindrance to the picnic.
The heavy bag was a hindrance on the hike.
The loud noise was a hindrance to study.

easy.def: Understanding something after it has happened.
examples: In hindsight, I was wrong.
Hindsight helps.
With hindsight, it was easy.

more.def: Understanding something only after it has happened.
examples: In hindsight, we should have packed an umbrella.
With hindsight, he would have chosen differently.
Hindsight tells you what to do next time.

easy.def: The metal part that lets a door swing open and shut.
examples: The door has a hinge.
The hinge squeaks.
Oil the hinge.

more.def: A metal joint that lets a door, a lid or a gate swing open and shut.
examples: The old door creaked on its rusty hinge.
The lid of the box was joined with a small metal hinge.
Dad put oil on the squeaky hinge.

easy.def: A small clue.
examples: Give me a hint.
The hint helped.
I need a hint.

more.def: A small piece of help that gives a clue without telling the whole answer.
examples: Give me a hint about the answer.
The teacher gave a hint about the next question.
A hint of smoke was in the air.

easy.def: The part at the side of your body, near your leg.
examples: I put my hands on my hips.
The hula hoop spun on her hips.
He hurt his hip.

more.def: The part of your body where your leg joins the rest of you, at the side below your waist.
examples: She put her hands on her hips.
He twisted his hips to spin the hula hoop.
Her hip hurt after she fell.

easy.def: A person with a free, peaceful way of life from the 1960s.
examples: The hippie wore flowers.
Hippies liked peace.
He dressed like a hippie.

more.def: A person from the 1960s and 1970s who wore flowery clothes and believed in peace and love.
examples: The hippie wore flowers in her hair.
Hippies often wore bright, loose clothes.
He dressed like a hippie for the party.

easy.def: A big animal with a wide mouth that lives near water in Africa.
examples: A hippo is big.
The hippo yawned.
We saw a hippo in the river.

more.def: A large African animal with thick skin and a very wide mouth that spends most of the day in water; short for hippopotamus.
examples: A hippo wallowed in the muddy river to keep cool.
The hippo opened its huge mouth and yawned.
Hippos spend the day in the water and come out to eat at night.

easy.def: A huge animal with thick skin that lives near water.
examples: A hippopotamus is big.
The hippopotamus swims.
We saw a hippopotamus.

more.def: A very large African animal with thick skin and a big mouth that spends much time in water.
examples: A hippopotamus rested in the muddy river.
The hippopotamus opened its huge mouth wide.
Hippopotamuses stay in water during the hot day.

easy.def: To pay someone to do a job.
examples: They hired a painter.
The shop hired a helper.
We hired a guide.

more.def: To pay someone to work for you.
examples: The restaurant hired a new cook.
We hired a guide to show us the cave.
The family hired a painter for the house.

easy.def: A word that shows something belongs to a boy or a man.
examples: That is his hat.
His dog is big.
Tom lost his shoe.

more.def: A word used to show that something belongs to or is connected with a boy, a man, or a male animal.
examples: My dad forgot his keys on the kitchen table.
The horse shook his mane in the wind.
Ravi finished his homework before dinner.

easy.def: To make a long "sss" sound.
examples: The snake hissed at us.
The cat hisses when it is scared.
Air hissed out of the tire.

more.def: To make a long, sharp "sss" sound, like a snake, a cat or air coming out of a small hole.
examples: The goose hissed and spread its wings when we came too close.
Steam hissed out of the kettle as the water boiled.
The balloon hissed as the air slowly escaped.

easy.def: A long "sss" sound.
examples: I heard a hiss in the grass.
The tire made a soft hiss.
The cat gave a loud hiss.

more.def: A long, sharp "sss" sound, like the one a snake or a leaking tire makes.
examples: We heard the hiss of a snake in the dry leaves.
The hiss of the steam told us that dinner was almost ready.
A hiss came from the old radiator when it warmed up.

easy.def: A person who studies the past.
examples: The historian wrote a book.
A historian knows old events.
The historian visited our class.

more.def: A person who studies and writes about what happened in the past.
examples: The historian wrote a book about the Civil War.
A historian visited our class.
The historian studied old letters.

easy.def: Important in history.
examples: It was a historic day.
A historic house.
We saw a historic place.

more.def: Important or famous in history.
examples: July fourth is a historic day for the country.
We toured a historic house built over two hundred years ago.
The team won a historic victory.

easy.def: Having to do with the past.
examples: It is a historical place.
A historical story.
We visited a historical site.

more.def: Having to do with history, or something that really happened in the past.
examples: The historical museum showed old maps.
The story is based on a historical event.
The museum has historical maps.

easy.def: What happened in the past.
examples: We learn history at school.
I read about the history of our town.
I love history.

more.def: The study of events in the past, or the events themselves.
examples: In history class, we learned about the first explorers.
The museum tells the history of our town.
Her grandmother knows the history of the family.

easy.def: To touch something hard with a quick move.
examples: I hit the ball.
The ball hit the wall.
She hit the drum.

more.def: To strike something with force, usually with your hand or an object.
examples: She hit the ball over the fence with a bat.
The rain hit the window with a loud tap.
He hit the drum in time with the music.

easy.def: To fasten with a hook.
examples: I hitch the horse.
Dad hitched the trailer.
She hitched the sled.

more.def: To fasten something to something else with a hook or rope.
examples: The farmer hitched the horse to the cart.
Dad hitched the trailer to the car.
She hitched her sled to the dog.

easy.def: To ask for a ride from strangers on the road.
examples: Never hitchhike.
He hitchhiked home.
They hitchhiked across the country.

more.def: To travel by asking drivers you do not know for a ride, which can be unsafe.
examples: It is not safe to hitchhike, so a child should never ask a stranger for a ride.
The character in the book hitchhiked across the country.
The two students hitchhiked to the next town.

easy.def: A player who hits the ball.
examples: She is a good hitter.
The hitter swung.
A strong hitter.

more.def: A player, especially in baseball, who hits the ball with a bat.
examples: She is the best hitter on our baseball team.
The hitter swung and sent the ball over the fence.
The pitcher struck out the next hitter.

easy.def: A home where bees live.
examples: Bees live in a hive.
The hive is busy.
The beekeeper checked the hive.

more.def: A home for bees, either a box made by a beekeeper or a nest that bees build themselves.
examples: Thousands of bees live together in the hive.
The beekeeper wore a special suit to open the hive.
Honey is stored in the hive in little wax cells.
